text: I saw a therapist for about six months who did a mix of CBT and somatic work. That helped with the panic. I used a breathing app daily. Limiting news consumption helped a lot. I haven't been back to a festival and I don't think I will.

Ich habe eine Verhaltenstherapie gemacht, in der es um meine Gesundheitsängste ging. Eine Atemtherapeutin hat mir auch geholfen, wieder Vertrauen in meinen Atem zu bekommen. Inzwischen geht es mir gut.

I've tried a lot and honestly most of it didn't help much.

I've seen three psychiatrists. I've tried sertraline, fluoxetine, lamotrigine, and naltrexone, which is sometimes used for DP. Lamotrigine maybe helped a tiny bit with the visuals. Nothing touched the depersonalisation. I've seen two therapists. The first did CBT and the second did a more trauma-focused approach. The second was kinder but I still feel the same.

I tried meditation, but focusing inward makes the DP worse. Mindfulness of the senses outdoors helps a bit, for a few minutes. Exercise helps a bit with my mood. I've cut out all substances.

Online communities for DP/DR have been both a help and a harm. Some people recovered and that gives me hope. Others are stuck for decades and that scares me.

I'm still struggling every day. I've mostly learned to live with it, but I wouldn't call that healing.
I started trauma therapy with EMDR about three months later. It took a long time but it helped me process the assault. My partner came to some sessions with me. We're doing much better now.

My facilitator offered two integration sessions as part of the service, which helped me make sense of the experience, especially the near-drowning memory. Then I found a therapist who works with somatic trauma, and we've been working on my breathing panic for about a year. I took adult swimming lessons with a very patient instructor. The first time I put my face in the water, I cried. Now I can swim lengths again. The panic attacks are rare now.
Talked to friends who use psychedelics, gave them up for a while. Did some mindfulness. It went away by itself after a few months.

I went to my GP eventually and was prescribed an antidepressant (citalopram). It helped a bit after a couple of months. I did a course of CBT through the NHS, which was okay but felt a bit generic. Running and joining a hiking group helped me meet new people. Still on the medication.

Ich habe einen Integrationskreis für Menschen mit schwierigen Psychedelika-Erfahrungen gefunden, der mir sehr geholfen hat. Später habe ich noch einige Stunden Psychotherapie gemacht. Viel Zeit in der Natur verbringen, tagsüber, hat geholfen, die Angst vor der Dunkelheit langsam abzubauen.
Told my mom the truth eventually, that helped.
Ich habe einige Stunden Therapie gemacht, die mir geholfen haben, die Scham zu verarbeiten. Die soziale Angst ist besser, aber ich vermeide immer noch große Feiern.
